Turning G into H deletes node C and edge A–C (accent in G) and inserts node E and edge D–E (accent in H): four edits at cost 1 each, so the distance is 4." width="100%"} Counts the node insertions, node deletions, edge insertions, and edge deletions needed to transform this graph into the other. By default the nodes are matched by label, which is fast; with `exact=True` the method instead searches every node correspondence for the cheapest edit path, as NetworkX's `graph_edit_distance()` does. In the default label-based mode, nodes are matched by label (an unlabelled node is represented by its ID as a string), and edges by the labels of their endpoints. A node whose label exists only in `other=` costs one node insertion and a node whose label exists only in the calling graph costs one node deletion; edges are counted the same way. Each count is multiplied by its cost and the products are summed into `distance`. Because the node correspondence is fixed by the labels, there is no search over possible node mappings: the method runs in linear time and is "approximate" only in the sense that it does not look for a cheaper relabelling. Two structurally identical graphs with different labels therefore get a large distance. This is useful for: - quantifying how far a network has moved between two snapshots or conditions - scoring a reconstructed network against a reference network on the same entities - ranking several candidate networks by how close they are to a target Edges follow the same rules as `edge_overlap()`: in undirected graphs `A--B` equals `B--A`, weights and attributes are ignored, and parallel edges count once. Edges attached to a deleted or inserted node are counted as separate edge edits as well. With `exact=True`, labels play no part: the distance is the minimum cost of any edit path that turns this graph into a graph isomorphic to `other=`, where each node and edge is either substituted by one in `other=`, deleted, or inserted. Substitutions are free unless `node_match=`, `edge_match=` or a substitution cost function says otherwise, so two structurally identical graphs are at distance `0`. The search is exponential in the worst case and is practical for graphs of up to about a dozen nodes; `upper_bound=` and `timeout=` keep larger comparisons in check. Use `optimal_edit_paths()` to see the edits themselves. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The target graph. The distance measures the cost of turning the calling graph into this one. It should normally have the same directedness as the calling graph. With the default unit costs the distance is symmetric, so swapping the graphs only swaps the insertion and deletion counts. [node_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Cost charged for each node insertion or deletion. The default is `1.0`. Set it to `0.0` to count only edge changes, or raise it to make changes to the node set weigh more than rewiring. With `exact=True` it is the default for `node_del_cost=` and `node_ins_cost=`. [edge_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Cost charged for each edge insertion or deletion. The default is `1.0`. Like `node_cost=`, this only scales the `distance` value; the individual counts in the result are unaffected. With `exact=True` it is the default for `edge_del_cost=` and `edge_ins_cost=`. [exact]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), match nodes by label. If `True`, compute the exact graph edit distance by searching over node correspondences. The remaining parameters apply only to the exact mode, and passing any of them without `exact=True` raises an error. [node_match]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], bool]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A function called as `node_match(attrs1, attrs2)` with the attribute dictionaries of a node of this graph and a node of `other=`, returning `True` if the two may be substituted for free. A substitution of non-matching nodes costs `1`. Ignored when `node_subst_cost=` is given. If neither is given, node attributes are ignored. [edge_match]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], bool]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Like `node_match=`, for the attribute dictionaries of two edges. An edge's dictionary holds its attributes plus its `"weight"` when it has one. [node_subst_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Functions returning the cost of substituting a node of this graph by a node of `other=` (called with both attribute dictionaries), deleting a node of this graph, and inserting a node of `other=` (each called with one attribute dictionary). Costs must be non-negative numbers. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `node_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `node_cost=`. [node_del_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Functions returning the cost of substituting a node of this graph by a node of `other=` (called with both attribute dictionaries), deleting a node of this graph, and inserting a node of `other=` (each called with one attribute dictionary). Costs must be non-negative numbers. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `node_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `node_cost=`. [node_ins_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Functions returning the cost of substituting a node of this graph by a node of `other=` (called with both attribute dictionaries), deleting a node of this graph, and inserting a node of `other=` (each called with one attribute dictionary). Costs must be non-negative numbers. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `node_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `node_cost=`. [edge_subst_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The same three functions for edges. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `edge_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `edge_cost=`. [edge_del_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The same three functions for edges. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `edge_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `edge_cost=`. [edge_ins_cost]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[dict, dict], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The same three functions for edges. Without them, a substitution costs `0` (or follows `edge_match=`) and a deletion or insertion costs `edge_cost=`. [roots]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[tuple]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A pair `(u, v)` of a node of this graph and a node of `other=` (IDs or labels) that are forced to correspond, for comparing rooted graphs. [upper_bound]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The largest distance to consider. If no edit path costs this much or less, the `distance` is `None`. [timeout]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A time limit in seconds, which must be positive. When it runs out the best distance found so far is returned, which may be larger than the true distance. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary with float values under these keys: - `distance`: the total cost. In the label-based mode this is `(node_insertions + node_deletions) * node_cost + (edge_insertions + edge_deletions) * edge_cost`. - `node_insertions`, `node_deletions`: the number of node labels found only in `other=` and only in the calling graph, respectively, or, with `exact=True`, the number of nodes inserted and deleted by the optimal edit path. - `edge_insertions`, `edge_deletions`: the number of edges found only in `other=` and only in the calling graph, respectively, or the edges inserted and deleted by the optimal edit path. With `exact=True` the dictionary also holds `node_substitutions` and `edge_substitutions`, the number of node and edge pairs the edit path maps onto each other (substitutions that cost nothing included). When no edit path is within `upper_bound=`, every value is `None`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an exact-mode parameter is given without `exact=True`, if (in exact mode) the graphs differ in directedness, a cost is negative or not a number, a root is not in its graph, or `timeout=` is not positive. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~edge_overlap`) : Compare edge sets with a Jaccard index. [](`~differential_edges`) : List which edges were added or removed. [](`~optimal_edit_paths`) : List every cheapest edit path. [](`~optimize_graph_edit_distance`) : Iterate over improving distance estimates. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The exact mode runs the depth-first branch-and-bound search of Abu-Aisheh et al. (2015), following NetworkX's `optimize_edit_paths()`: each step maps one more node of this graph to a node of `other=` (or deletes or inserts it), settles the edges between mapped nodes, and prunes a branch as soon as its cost plus a lower bound on the remaining edits, from linear sum assignments solved with the Hungarian algorithm, reaches the best complete path found so far. Self-loops can only be substituted by self-loops on the matching node; NetworkX lets a loop stand in for any edge at the matched nodes and can then report a distance below the true one. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Turning `g` into `h` requires deleting node `C` and its edge `A--C`, then inserting node `E` and the edge `D--E`. That is one edit of each kind, for a total distance of `4.0`: ::: {#e63c2436 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "D"), ("A", "C")]) ) h = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) g.graph_edit_distance(h) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'edge_insertions': 1.0, 'edge_deletions': 1.0, 'node_insertions': 1.0, 'node_deletions': 1.0, 'distance': 4.0} ``` ::: ::: The costs only change how the counts are weighted. With `node_cost=0.0` the two node edits are free, so only the two edge edits remain: ::: {#d0596176 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.graph_edit_distance(h, node_cost=0.0)["distance"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2.0 ``` ::: ::: Both graphs are in fact four-node paths (`C--A--B--D` and `A--B--D--E`). The exact mode ignores the labels, and relabelling nodes is free, so every node and edge is substituted and the distance is `0`: ::: {#30138283 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.graph_edit_distance(h, exact=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'distance': 0.0, 'node_insertions': 0.0, 'node_deletions': 0.0, 'node_substitutions': 4.0, 'edge_insertions': 0.0, 'edge_deletions': 0.0, 'edge_substitutions': 3.0} ``` ::: ::: The exact distance between a six-node cycle and a seven-node wheel is `7`: one node (the hub) and its six spokes are inserted: ::: {#cdeace3a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} cycle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) wheel = ec.Graph().add_wheel_graph(7) cycle.graph_edit_distance(wheel, exact=True)["distance"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 7.0 ``` ::: ::: Attributes enter through the match and cost functions. Here substituting atoms of different elements is not free, so the two chains differ by one substitution: ::: {#2e34b38e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} a = ec.Graph().add_nodes([("a1", {"el": "C"}), ("a2", {"el": "O"})]) a.add_edges([("a1", "a2")]) b = ec.Graph().add_nodes([("b1", {"el": "C"}), ("b2", {"el": "N"})]) b.add_edges([("b1", "b2")]) a.graph_edit_distance(b, exact=True, node_match=lambda x, y: x["el"] == y["el"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` {'distance': 1.0, 'node_insertions': 0.0, 'node_deletions': 0.0, 'node_substitutions': 2.0, 'edge_insertions': 0.0, 'edge_deletions': 0.0, 'edge_substitutions': 1.0} ``` ::: :::
